cells.tense: You are naming the way things run, right here, while everyone can hear it.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Take the next step you've been picturing for how things run here, and do it the same day you picture it.
cells.core:
You keep a direction without forcing it. Around you the loose ends get tied into something people can actually use, and you do it warmly, while the thing is still small enough to shape. Nobody has to guess what today is for. That's the working part, and it holds because the fire is tended and the structure sits around it.

What hasn't happened is a yes to the next step you keep picturing. Picture it plainly, then take one real step toward it the same day. No announcement, no asking anyone first. The shape you have now will shift a little when you do, and those who live inside it can handle the shift better than you think.

cells.tense: You will have the whole arrangement settled before anyone has said a word.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Before you set the next rule here, tell the real reason to the person it affects, once, plainly, at a size they can take in.
cells.core:
Where you keep the direction, you're arranging things ahead of time now. Every loose end gets a rule before it lands, every future morning gets a plan, and it holds without wobbling. The hold is real. What it costs is that the structure arrives complete, and those living inside it are reading a decision they didn't get to hear make sense.

Pick the next thing you're about to organize here and give the actual reason for it to the person it touches. Once, plainly, at a size they can take in, then let the answer land where it lands. A plan told early is still a plan; it just gets to be lived in.

cells.tense: You were standing at the point where you would have named how it all runs, and the ground already moved.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Find one old arrangement here that has already finished, end it, and leave the space it frees open.
cells.core:
Where the way things run gets named, that part is happening back past where you're standing. You're living inside dispositions that got settled without you, and nobody asks you to open them again. You keep going and the shape holds, but the part of you that decides what a today is for has gone quiet. You're here, and you're not setting anything here.

Look at what's already arranged and find one piece that has finished. End it on purpose, then leave the space it frees open for a week without filling it. What's done is done; what's left will tell you what it wants.

cells.tense: You are already deciding how this will run, and you're handing the credit to circumstance.
cells.act: force the change into reality by steady effort
cells.ask: Put tomorrow's shape here in one line where you'll see it, and hold that line through the week without rearranging it.
cells.core:
You name how things run here, and if someone asked, it just worked out that way. The mornings have their order, the work has a rhythm, and every few days the whole thing moves a degree — gently, without a meeting. Those moves come from you. They get filed under luck and timing, and the arrangement keeps drifting in the direction you were already steering it.

Pick one of the moves you keep making and say it out as a decision: tomorrow's shape, one line, somewhere you'll pass it. Hold that line through the week and don't take it apart. It'll probably need adjusting by Friday; leave your fingerprints on it anyway.
